graphtheory.name: Graph Theory: Connections Define Structure
graphtheory.truth: Everything is a graph if you squint hard enough.
graphtheory.qfep_connection: Graphs are pure relation — nodes are identity, edges are connection. The F-term lives in structure (spanning trees, shortest paths); the E-term in randomness (random graphs, percolation). Flow algorithms optimize the F↔E boundary.
graphtheory.description: Nodes and edges — the mathematics of connection. From Königsberg bridges to network flow, graph theory asks: what can you reach, what's connected, and what's the best path? Each map combines related algorithms into one explorable space.
learning_objectives: Graphs as abstract representations of relationship
Force-directed layout as physics applied to structure
Optimization on graphs — spanning trees, flow, matching
content: GT_Foundations: Königsberg Bridge problem + graph space exploration — what IS a graph?
GT_Layout: Force-directed graph layout in 2D and 3D — letting physics arrange structure
GT_Pathfinding: Finding paths through graphs — the traversal problem
GT_Network_Analysis: Network structure, flow, and analysis
GT_Connectivity: Tarjan's + Kosaraju's + topological sort — what's connected to what, in what order
GT_Spanning_Trees: Minimum spanning tree — the lightest skeleton
GT_Flow: Push-relabel + Karger's — maximum flow and minimum cut

merge_plan._note: Maps created by merging interactables from original 14 maps
